text:
maya: ran a few nsys + perfetto runs against the kv-cache ramp yesterday, dumping results here. noticing non-trivial tracer overhead on hot-paths, want opinions on safe thresholds to run in prod :thinking_face:
samir: can you paste the exact commands you ran?
maya: sure — for full GPU/KERNEL timelines i used:
```
nsys profile -o out_full --trace=cuda,cudnn --sample=none --capture-range=limited --capture-range-start=dispatch --capture-range-end=complete 
    --sample-freq=0 --force-overwrite --cpuctx on --delay 2 --duration 60 
./run-inference-loadtest --model=v2-quant --concurrency 64 --qps 400
```
maya: and for lightweight sampling runs i toggled to:
```
nsys profile -o out_sample --trace=cuda --sample=cpu --sample-freq=1000 --duration 60 
./run-inference-loadtest --model=v2-quant --concurrency 64 --qps 400
```
maya: raw high-level numbers: full-trace walltime increased ~11% on average (GPU kernel walltime measurable), p99 latency +18ms. sampling run increased walltime ~1.7% and p99 +3ms. KV-cache hit-rate dropped ~2% under full trace (likely because tracing serialized small operations).
kev: ok that's inline with expectations. nsys full capture is heavy. interesting that kv hit-rate moved — maybe tracing changes scheduling and cache eviction pressure.
jun: did you see different impact by sequence length? long seqs tend to dominate kernel time so overhead is relatively smaller there.
maya: yes — for short sequences (<=64 tokens) the relative overhead was worst: full trace +15% walltime; for >512 tokens it was only +4%.
samir: have we confirmed the overhead comes from the profiler hooking into memcpy/kernel launches and causing serialization? any nv-nsight logs?
maya: looked at kernel timelines, saw increased gaps between launches, a lot of tiny kernels got stretched. hypothesis: the capture path forces sync points for accurate timelines.
perf-bot: uploaded artifacts: https://ci.redwood/inference/artifacts/2001234567/ — includes nsys timelines and perfetto .pb files
kev: what about sampling granularity? you used --sample-freq=1000 which is coarse. How many samples did you collect?
maya: approx 120 samples across 60s run on the sampler config. gave us rough hotspots (softmax, rotary kernels) but not precise kernel durations.
samir: could we do hybrid: sample on GPU kernels but full on a tiny window triggered by anomalies? i.e., baseline sampling, then short full capture for traces that exceed p99 threshold.
jun: agree — guardrail idea: only allow full captures if request latency > trace_threshold AND trace-quota on host available. throttle full captures to 1 per 10k reqs or 1 per hour per-host.
kev: add a cold-start-only full capture mode too. KV-cache cold misses are interesting for ramp scenarios. main goal is to capture cold cache kernel mix.
maya: good call. for KV-cache warm/cold experiments i toggled cache-priming flags and saw that a full trace changes the priming pattern (makes it slower), so full traces bias the experiment. need to avoid biasing A/B tests.
samir: operational limits: 1) cap concurrent full-traces per host 2) only run full-trace on canary/Dedicated for first rollout 3) sampling default for prod 4) emergency full-trace when human approves.
maya: rough numbers for guardrails proposal:
- sampling default: trace-rate = 1/1000 requests, expected overhead ~<2%
- short full-window capture: 5s full trace triggered when p99 > baseline + 20ms, limited to 1/hr/host, overhead spike ~10-15% during capture
- long full capture: diagnostic for SRE only, require explicit opt-in, block on rollout policy, no auto-run in prod

kev: please validate those numbers across instance types. a100 vs h100 behavior differs — kernel launch overhead relative to kernel time changes.
jun: also factor in batching heuristics: if the capture changes scheduling, it can change batch composition. for slot-based batching we saw batch sizes shrink by 5% under full trace, which partly explains p99 increases.
maya: next steps i propose:
1) implement sampling-first pipeline: default sampler + auto-rollback to short full-window only when sampler flags a hotspot
2) add per-host full-trace quota and a global ramp control in the console
3) run cross-hardware validation (A100/H100) and sequence-length sweep to quantify delta numbers
4) document guardrails in runbooks and make tracer artifacts auto-upload to CI links

samir: +1. also add an experiment annotation so we can filter traces that were collected under sampling vs full so we don't mix them in evals.
kev: i'll own parts 2 and 3. jonathan can pair on the console bits.
jun: i'll help write the runbook text outlining safe opt-in flow for oncall.
maya: i'll open a PR with the sampling-first detector and the instrumentation toggles. will include a small emulated run to show we don't bias canary results.
deploy-bot: canary rollout executed: infra/canary/v2-quant @ 2026-03-18T15:02:13Z :truck:
maya: noted. aiming to have initial sampling-first roll by EOD tomorrow. any objections?
kev: none from me. keep the full-trace default off for prod.
samir: sg. thanks maya — this looks like a practical, safe plan. :thumbsup:
